# Free simplex affine neutrality with noncanonical vertex caps, all dimensions

This is a conditional rigidity theorem for one source simplex and one regular minimal critical circuit. It does not assume that arbitrary mixed bodies have a free source or one covering witness. Its sharp constant is Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d, d>=1. The planar scalar parameterization is recorded separately in `candidate 5f9c1392e667219d`; the inequality part of that note is subsumed by the theorem below.

## 1. Statement and exact neutrality assumption

Let K=conv(v_0,...,v_d) be a d-dimensional simplex, d>=1, with volume V>0. Let y in int K. For j=0,...,d let H_j={x:u_j dot(x-y)>=0}, with unit u_j, be a proper closed halfspace. Assume H_j contains v_j strictly and no other vertex strictly. Boundary contacts with other vertices are allowed initially. Assume the u_j span R^d and have a minimal positive dependence

    sum_j rho_j u_j=0, rho_j>0,
    dim ker[u_0 ... u_d]=1.                         (1)

Write U_j=|K intersect H_j|, E_j=K intersect boundary H_j, S_j=H_(d-1)(E_j)>0, and g_j for the centroid of E_j. For d=1 use counting measure, so each E_j is the single point y.

Let theta_j>0 with sum theta_j=1 and beta>0. Put W=sum theta_j 1_Hj on the boundary of K. Suppose the source response is neutral under every affine vector field: for all a in R^d and every real d by d matrix B,

    integral_(boundary K) [a+B(x-y)] dot n_K(x)
                                 [W(x)-beta] dH_(d-1)(x)=0.  (2)

For a polytope this is a sum of ordinary facet integrals; facet intersections have zero (d-1)-measure. Independent signed affine facet neutrality implies(2). Thus actual freedom under arbitrary separate facet tilts is sufficient, but is stronger than the affine-field hypothesis needed here.

Then

    beta>=Gamma_d.                                           (3)

For d>=2 equality holds exactly when y is the centroid, every cap is the canonical vertex cap with section parallel to its opposite facet, and theta_j=1/(d+1). For d=1, beta=1/2 for every y consistent with(2), and no centroid conclusion is asserted.

No convex-potential inequality is required for this theorem. Nor is beta replaced by an own-fiber normalized cap mass: it is the same response parameter appearing in(2).

## 2. Translations, homotheties, and general linear fields

Gauss–Green on K intersect H_j gives, for any affine field X,

    integral_(boundary K) 1_Hj X dot n_K
       = integral_(K intersect H_j) div X
                              + integral_(E_j) X dot u_j.    (4)

The cut face has outward normal -u_j, which gives the displayed PLUS sign after moving its flux to the other side. Intersections of that face with original facets have lower dimension and do not contribute. All E_j have positive proper coarea because their planes pass through int K.

For the constant field X=a, equation(2) and(4) yield

    sum_j theta_j S_j u_j=0.

By(1), there is c>0 such that

    theta_j S_j=c rho_j.                                    (5)

For X=x-y, its cut-face flux is zero because u_j dot(x-y)=0 on E_j, while div X=d. Consequently

    sum_j theta_j U_j=beta V.                               (6)

For X=B(x-y), formula(4) gives

    integral_(boundary K) 1_Hj X dot n_K
         =tr(B)U_j+S_j u_j dot B(g_j-y).

Use(6) to cancel the trace terms in(2), and then use(5). Since B is arbitrary,

    sum_j rho_j (g_j-y)u_j^T=0.                             (7)

For every coordinate of g_j-y, equation(7) gives a coefficient vector in the one-dimensional kernel from(1). Hence all displacements g_j-y are the SAME vector w. Each g_j lies on its own cut plane through y, so u_j dot w=0 for every j. Their span is R^d, thus w=0. We have proved

    g_j=y for EVERY j.                                      (8)

This is the decisive geometric consequence of actual affine neutrality.

## 3. Source barycentrics and exclusion of contact degeneracies

Write y_j>0 for the barycentric coordinates of y, with sum y_j=1. The section E_j is the (d-1)-simplex whose vertices lie on edges v_jv_k, k!=j, at fractions t_jk in(0,1] measured from v_j. This remains valid when a cut passes through an excluded vertex: the corresponding fraction is1. Its barycentric centroid coordinates away from j are t_jk/d. Equation(8) therefore forces

    t_jk=d y_k, k!=j.                                     (9)

For d>=2 every index k occurs away from some j, so d y_k<=1. The same holds for d=1 because y_k<1. Define

    r_j=1-d y_j>=0, sum_j r_j=1.                           (10)

Normalize each affine cap margin to take value1 at its isolated vertex. In barycentric coordinates lambda its exact expression is

    F_j=lambda_j-sum_(k!=j) [(1-d y_k)/(d y_k)]lambda_k
       =lambda_j/(d y_j)-sum_k [r_k/(d y_k)]lambda_k.       (11)

At y this is zero. Equation(10) gives

    sum_j r_j F_j=0.                                      (12)

The gradients of the F_j are positive scalar multiples of the u_j. They thus have a one-dimensional kernel with a strictly positive vector, by(1). The nonzero nonnegative kernel vector r in(12) must be proportional to that vector. Hence

    r_j>0 for every j.                                    (13)

This excludes ALL t_jk=1 contact branches after the fact. No strict incidence or general-position assumption was inserted into the argument.

## 4. Exact response formula

Let q_j=U_j/V be the own-fiber cap fraction. It is the product of its d edge fractions, so by(9)

    q_j=product_(k!=j)(d y_k)
       =d^d (product_k y_k)/y_j.                         (14)

The margin F_j has height1 at v_j and zero on its section. The corresponding Euclidean pyramid height is1/|grad F_j|. The pyramid volume formula gives its RAW-threshold coarea

    C_j:=S_j/|grad F_j|=d U_j=d V q_j.                  (15)

The positive dependence for the unit normals is proportional to r_j|grad F_j| by(12). Thus(5) makes theta_j proportional to r_j/q_j. Normalization and(6) give

    theta_j=(r_j/q_j)/(sum_h r_h/q_h),
    beta=1/(sum_j r_j/q_j)
         =d^d product_j y_j/[1-d sum_j y_j^2]
         =product_j(1-r_j)/[1-sum_j r_j^2].             (16)

Every denominator is positive by(13): r belongs to the open probability simplex, so sum r_j^2<1. Formula(16) tracks the exact constant without an asymptotic loss.

## 5. Sharp symmetric inequality

For a positive probability vector r of length d+1 put

    f(r)=product_j(1-r_j)/[1-sum_j r_j^2].

For d=1, direct substitution r_0+r_1=1 gives f=1/2 identically.

For d>=2, compute for i!=j

    partial_i log f-partial_j log f
     =(r_i-r_j)[2/(1-sum r^2)-1/((1-r_i)(1-r_j))].       (17)

The numerator in brackets, after taking its positive common denominator, is

    2(1-r_i)(1-r_j)-(1-sum r^2)
       =(sum_(k!=i,j)r_k)^2+sum_(k!=i,j)r_k^2>0.        (18)

Keeping r_i+r_j fixed, moving the larger coordinate toward the smaller therefore strictly decreases f until they agree. Successively average a largest and a smallest coordinate. All coordinates stay between the initial positive minimum and maximum below1. The variance around the uniform vector decreases by half the square of their difference; therefore their range tends to zero, and the vectors converge to the uniform vector. Continuity gives the minimum there. If the initial vector was nonuniform, the first averaging strictly decreases f, so equality is impossible.

At the uniform vector r_j=1/(d+1),

    f=(d/(d+1))^(d+1)/(d/(d+1))=Gamma_d.

Thus(3) follows, with equality exactly at uniform r. Equations(9),(10),(16) then give y_j=1/(d+1), t_jk=d/(d+1), and uniform theta. These are precisely the canonical centroid caps. Conversely those caps and weights satisfy(2), as follows either by(4) or by their facet mass and first-moment equations.

## 6. Conditional application to a mixed minimum

Suppose an actual local minimum of normalized mixed depth has one selected regular minimal circuit covering ALL deepest base planes, and finite persistent slack covers at the other bases. Let its source fiber be a freely affinely deformable simplex, with one cap isolating each vertex. Regularity excludes positive-area supporting coincidences on any measured fiber; other fibers may otherwise have arbitrary proper/full/empty statuses.

For every signed source affine motion, the equal-budget circuit response gives an actual upper comparison for the global depth. Local minimality makes the normalized first response nonnegative; applying this to both signs makes it zero. Thus(2) holds, with theta the actual response weights computed from FULL proper coarea across all fibers. The proof above then uses the SOURCE coareas S_j in(5), inferred from translation neutrality; these must not be confused with the full coareas which originally define theta.

The theorem forces beta>=Gamma_d and excludes beta<Gamma_d/2^n under these hypotheses. The strict finite-extreme support-inclusion condition in the root free-source note is one sufficient realization of the required affine freedom.

For multiple witnesses, local minimality does not separately neutralize each circuit. For supporting coincidences, the common allocation affects both weights and traces. If the caps do not isolate distinct simplex vertices, formula(9) does not follow from(8). Those unresolved settings are not replaced by the present theorem.
